title: Security posture discovery with Titan Health
summary: High-level security discovery focused on SOC2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS options, and private (VPC/on-prem) deployment considerations. Customer is leaning toward a Dedicated or Private deployment due to PHI concerns and retention requirements; asked for SOC2/ISO docs, architecture diagram for private control plane, and benchmark plan for latency/cost. Next steps agreed: deliver attestation docs, architecture diagram, pricing and benchmark plan; follow-up call with DevOps to scope pilot.
topics: Encryption at-rest and in-transit / KMS/HSM options
Data residency and retention policy for PHI
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, we'll get started. I'm Maya from Redwood, our SE Diego and CSM Priya are with me.
[00:00:12] Alex Park: Yep, Alex here, CISO at Titan Health. Appreciate you fitting this in. Quick note, we have PHI and strict retention rules so security is, uh, top priority.
[00:00:25] Maya Chen: Totally, that's what we want to focus on today — SOC two and ISO questions, SSO and RBAC, audit logs, KMS, and the private options. Diego can dive into architecture.
[00:00:38] Diego Ramos: Hi all, Diego Ramos, Redwood SE. I'll try to keep it pragmatic — networking, encryption, and what Dedicated/Private looks like operationally.
[00:00:47] Jory Patel: Hi, Jory here. From ML side we care about latency and cost but security is a blocker. If we can't meet compliance we won't get approval.
[00:00:58] Samira Khan: Samira, DevOps — we'll need APIs for provisioning and IaC modules, also SCIM for user sync.
[00:01:10] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: 1) current security/regulatory posture at Titan, 2) deployment constraints, 3) specific questions on attestations and controls, 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:01:22] Alex Park: Yes. We're SOC2 Type II in scope, pursuing ISO 27001 earlier this year. We need vendor attestations and evidence of controls for vendors that handle PHI. Also SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning, role-based access, and audit trails retained for 7 years — that's a hard requirement.
[00:01:44] Maya Chen: Understood. For SOC2, we can provide our Type II report and SOC bridge letters. For ISO 27001 we have the cert and scope doc, I'll send the attestation.
[00:01:56] Alex Park: When you say "send" can you provide redacted copies and an evidence pack? Our audit team will want to review specific controls.
[00:02:06] Priya Nair: Yep we typically provide redacted SOC2 + control narrative and an FAQ that maps controls to our product features. We'll attach that in the follow-up.
[00:02:16] Jory Patel: On encryption — do you support customer-managed keys? We need KMS/HSM for key separation.
[00:02:25] Diego Ramos: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS integration and HSM-backed key material for secrets. For Dedicated there's an option to integrate with customer KMS via our key-wrapping flow, though the control plane for hosted is managed by Redwood; in Private you get control plane in your VPC.
[00:02:44] Samira Khan: So for Dedicated, logs and data — where are they stored? Are audit logs accessible to us?
[00:02:52] Diego Ramos: Audit logs are shipped to a customer-designated sink for Dedicated and Private — S3, GCS, or a SIEM via syslog/HTTP forward. For Hosted plans we retain logs but we can provide exports and field-level redaction.
[00:03:08] Alex Park: Field-level redaction — can we redact PHI before logs leave our environment? That would be ideal.
[00:03:16] Diego Ramos: Yes, we have prefix caching and response filtering hooks. For Private deployment you can configure agents to redact fields before logs are forwarded; for Dedicated we can set up a pipeline with PII redaction if we have agreement in the pilot.
[00:03:32] Maya Chen: On SSO — we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC supports custom roles and attribute-based checks.
[00:03:42] Samira Khan: Any quirks with our Okta setup? We use Okta + SCIM.
[00:03:48] Diego Ramos: Okta is a first-class integration — we map groups to roles, support JIT and SCIM provisioning. Sometimes customers ask about SCIM delta sync timing — typical is ~2–5 minutes depending on SCIM events.
[00:04:00] Jory Patel: Audit retention 7 years — that's longer than most defaults, any cost or storage caveats?
[00:04:09] Diego Ramos: Storage cost is mostly pass-through if you're storing in your own S3/GCS. For hosted where we store on behalf of customers, we have long-term retention tiers and can provide cold storage at reduced rates; we'll include estimates in the pricing.
[00:04:23] Alex Park: About data residency — we process in NA but need EU data to remain in EU for a specific product line. Can you restrict region processing?
[00:04:33] Maya Chen: Yes, policy-based routing available. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can pin workloads to region and set routing policies to avoid cross-border egress.
[00:04:44] Samira Khan: Network wise — will we need VPNs, or is peering supported?
[00:04:49] Diego Ramos: Both. Private control plane in your VPC uses VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. VPN is also supported for on-prem. We'll send a network diagram in the follow-up.
[00:05:02] Lena Ortiz: On legal side, do you sign a BAA? We handle PHI and need a BAA plus data processing addendum.
[00:05:10] Maya Chen: We do sign BAAs for customers handling PHI; our legal team will send a standard DPA/BAA and can negotiate terms.
[00:05:18] Alex Park: Great. About model data — does Redwood store prompts and responses by default? We need control over retention and the ability to opt-out of storing prompts for PHI workloads.
[00:05:29] Diego Ramos: By default we have ephemeral request logs for optimization and debugging, but customers can opt into longer retention. For PHI workloads on Private or Dedicated you can disable persistent storage and keep only aggregated telemetry.
[00:05:44] Jory Patel: Are weights or model checkpoints ever uploaded to Redwood? We want to verify there's no exfil of model artifacts.
[00:05:50] Diego Ramos: Models are hosted by you for Private; for Dedicated we manage model artifacts on our isolated infra but we have strict operational controls and ACLs. We can provide a model handling checklist in the artifact pack.
[00:06:03] Samira Khan: Regarding logging — do you provide immutable audit logs for compliance?
[00:06:09] Diego Ramos: We support append-only logs and can ship to an S3 bucket with Object Lock for immutability; also forward to your SIEM for retention.
[00:06:19] Alex Park: How about incident response and breach notification timelines?
[00:06:23] Maya Chen: Standard contractually bound 72-hour notification for incidents, and we provide a post-incident report and remediation plan.
[00:06:31] Jory Patel: Latency — for our primary use cases we need 95th percentile < 200ms for short prompts. What's realistic on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[00:06:40] Diego Ramos: On Dedicated with pinned GPUs and optimized kernels we typically hit sub-200ms for short sequences; Hosted can vary with multi-tenant peaks. We'll propose a Dedicated pilot with perf SLAs for the benchmark.
[00:06:53] Maya Chen: To recap so far: you need SOC2/ISO docs and control narrative, architecture/network diagram for Private, proof of KMS/HSM support, audit log export configuration, and a benchmark plan for Dedicated. Anything else?
[00:07:07] Alex Park: Also legal wants the DPA/BAA and confirmation on data deletion policies and canned retention settings.
[00:07:15] Lena Ortiz: Correct — plus liability caps and subprocessor list.
[00:07:19] Maya Chen: We'll include the subprocessor list and our standard limits; legal can flag redlines.
[00:07:24] Samira Khan: For the pilot, we want a scriptable harness to run 10k requests/min for 2 hours to check throughput and lat. Can you provide that?
[00:07:33] Diego Ramos: Absolutely — I'll prepare a benchmark harness and sample IaC to spin up the Dedicated environment. We'll also include guide for running tests and collecting traces.
[00:07:45] Jory Patel: Any known compliance gaps in the Hosted product for PHI?
[00:07:50] Diego Ramos: Hosted is SOC2 compliant and we have controls, but for PHI we typically recommend Dedicated or Private to reduce shared-tenant risk and give you control over key management and retention.
[00:08:03] Alex Park: Understood. A couple clarifying questions on RBAC — can you bind roles to Okta group attributes and also support attribute-based access controls?
[00:08:12] Maya Chen: Yes, RBAC maps to SAML attributes and Okta groups; we also support attribute-based policies in Private for fine-grained enforcement (e.g., restrict export scope by project tag).
[00:08:25] Samira Khan: Backup/DR — if we go Private on-prem, how are backups handled? Are those encrypted with customer keys?
[00:08:33] Diego Ramos: Backups are encrypted at-rest; for Private we can integrate with your KMS so keys are customer-controlled. For on-prem we provide options to store backups in customer-controlled storage.
[00:08:45] Alex Park: Any SOC 3 or public attestations we can point to?
[00:08:50] Priya Nair: We have a public SOC3 summary and our security whitepaper that outlines controls; I'll link both.
[00:08:58] Jory Patel: Who would be the primary contact during the pilot? We need an SE and an ops lead.
[00:09:05] Maya Chen: Diego will be your SE lead, and Priya will be CSM for the pilot. I'll be the AE owner for contract and pricing.
[00:09:12] Alex Park: Timeline — we want to present to the execs in 3 weeks. Can you get docs and pricing within a week so we can prep?
[00:09:19] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll send the attestation pack, network diagram, pricing estimate and benchmark plan by next Thursday.
[00:09:27] Lena Ortiz: Also request: redactable SOC2 and named contact for legal to negotiate the BAA.
[00:09:34] Maya Chen: Noted.
[00:09:36] Diego Ramos: Quick note — sometimes transcriptions show "K-V cache" or "KV cache" interchangeably; just to avoid confusion in the docs we'll standardize naming.
[00:09:46] Samira Khan: Ha, appreciate that.
[00:09:49] Maya Chen: Any final questions?
[00:09:52] Alex Park: No, that covers it. We'll expect the follow-up.
[00:09:58] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — recap and next steps in the follow-up email.
[00:10:02] -- call ended --
next_steps: Send redacted SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts + control narrative
Share network/architecture diagram for Private control plane and Dedicated setup
Provide benchmark plan and sample harness for Dedicated pilot
Send DPA/BAA and subprocessor list; nominate legal contact for negotiations
Provide pricing estimate for 3-month Dedicated pilot
action_items: Maya Chen - Send SOC2/ISO artifacts and control narrative - 2027-10-04
Diego Ramos - Prepare benchmark harness, sample IaC, and network diagram - 2027-10-07
Priya Nair - Share SOC3 summary and security whitepaper links - 2027-10-04
Alex Park - Provide Titan data retention policy and territories for residency - 2027-10-05
Lena Ortiz - Review DPA/BAA and flag redlines - 2027-10-11
